headlines: Treasury sanctions 17 tankers linked to Iran's 'shadow fleet' in economic pressure campaign
Trump: U.S. won't attack Iran before midterms
Rising oil prices, falling technology stocks and reversing bond yields keep Wall Street unsettled
Judge Sides With Importers to Expand Trump Tariff Refund Fight
Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before midterm election
Oil prices rise after reports White House weighing Iran strikes

cards.hearing: You may be hearing about Iran, tanker sanctions, and oil prices moving this week.
cards.why: Oil is the stuff that becomes gas and diesel, so when it moves, that can nudge what it costs to fill up the car or get a truck of groceries to the store.
cards.but: But oil swinging around a geopolitical headline is not new, and it is not a reason to redo a long-term plan.
cards.story: Picture a family road trip where the price at one gas station jumps for a week. You still take the trip. You just notice the sign a little more at that one stop.
say: We see the headline on oil, and we are not changing the plan over it.
Gas prices can bounce around news like this without bouncing your long-term plan.

cards.hearing: You may hear that stocks, especially technology stocks, slipped a bit this week.
cards.why: Weeks like this can feel unsettling because the moves show up fast in a headline, even when nothing in your actual plan has changed.
cards.but: But a softer week is a normal part of investing, not a signal to make a big move.
cards.story: Picture a long hiking trail with a few rocky patches. You slow down, you watch your step, but you do not turn around and drive home. The trail still gets you where you are going.
say: This week was a little rocky. That is part of the trail, not the end of it.
We stay on the path. A soft week does not change where we are headed.

cards.hearing: You may hear that interest rates eased a little this week.
cards.why: Rates touch things like borrowing costs, so small moves there can show up in everyday money decisions, even small ones.
cards.but: But small moves in rates happen often, and your plan was built to handle that back-and-forth.
cards.story: Picture a thermostat that gets nudged down a notch. You feel a small difference in the room, but nobody moves out of the house over it.
say: Interest rates eased a touch this week. The house, meaning your plan, stays the same.
Small rate moves are normal. We built your plan expecting them.
